properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 3 at 12:47PM MST until September 3 at 3:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Graham County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 345 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1247 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Aravaipa Creek, Deer Creek, Kennedy Falls Wash, Long Hollow,
Paddys River, Sycamore Creek, Sheep Wash, Two E Wash, Klondyke
Wash, Fourmile Creek, Crazy Horse Wash, Oak Creek, Gardner Creek,
Squaw Creek, Turkey Creek, Rattlesnake Creek and Fresnal Wash.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Klondyke.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances. Take extra precautions if you work or spend time
outside. When possible reschedule strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion

possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety

in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 3 at 11:18AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Central Interior-Nenana-Two Rivers-Middle Yukon Valley-Upper Koyukuk
Valley-Upper Chena River Valley-Fairbanks Metro Area-Goldstream
Valley and Nenana Hills-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Dalton Highway
Summits-Chatanika River Valley-White Mountains and High Terrain South
of the Yukon River-Eielson AFB and Salcha

Areas of 1 to 2.5 inches of rainfall are expected over the next 48
hours due to an atmospheric river. Average return intervals of 2 to 5
years is possible throughout much of the central and western interior
through the weekend. Isolated areas could potentially see heavy
rainfall more in line with 10 to even 25 year return intervals,
resulting in significant rises in the smaller headwater streams that
feed the Koyukuk and Middle Yukon Rivers. While there are no
immediate concerns for the main stem rivers in the area, they will
also see significant rises in water levels through the week as a
result of the expected heavy rainfall with sandbars potentially
becoming covered with water.

Across the Chena River basin, moderate to heavy rainfall of up to 1.5
inches is expected. This will also result in rises along the Chena
and Little Chena rivers. At this time flooding is not expected, but
should the focus for heaviest rainfall shift further east with time,
this could change.

Rainfall rates are expected to decrease by Sunday afternoon across
most of the area.

roads or structures is NOT expected.

Saturday, 6pm on Sunday, 7pm on Monday, and 8pm on Tuesday.

such conditions, stay off the rocks. Follow advice from local
officials. Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of

rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Enhanced beach
erosion will occur. Flooding of sea water is likely, around the
time of high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such
as parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Significant damage to
roads or structures is NOT expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will occur around 5pm on
Saturday, 6pm on Sunday, 7pm on Monday, and 8pm on Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks. Follow advice from local
officials. Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
early Saturday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.8
feet on 02/12/1966.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 3 at 1:14PM CDT until September 3 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS North Platte NE
properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS LIKELY IN THE NORTHEASTERN
PANHANDLE AND NORTHWESTERN SANDHILLS THIS AFTERNOON INTO THE EARLY
EVENING HOURS...

The National Weather Service in North Platte has issued a Red
Flag Warning for low relative humidity and gusty winds, which is
in effect until 8 PM MDT this evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 204 Eastern
Panhandle/Crescent Lake NWR.

* TIMING...through 8 PM MDT.

* WINDS...West 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph. Gusts up to
35 MPH are possible in Sheridan and northwestern Cherry County.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 14 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 95.

* LIGHTNING...None expected.

* IMPACTS...Any fire starts have a high probability to spread
rapidly and be difficult to control.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 4 at 3:50AM ChST until September 4 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, hazardous surf of 7 to
10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...West facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Pulses in the southwesterly monsoon along the

from the southwest to the northwest to the Marianas today.
properties.instruction:

dangerous surf conditions.

If caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against
the current. If able, swim in a direction following the
shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave
for help.

Northeastern San Jacinto County in southeastern Texas...
East Central Trinity County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 330 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Texas...

forecast.

* WHERE...Menard Creek near Rye.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 28.0 feet, major lowland flooding begins with
widespread inundation of the floodplain in the vicinity of the
gage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 17.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:15 AM CDT Thursday was 26.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 27.3 feet
this evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 27.2
feet on 03/30/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Brazos, Grimes, Houston, Madison, Montgomery, Northern

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

Polk, San Jacinto, Montgomery, and Trinity Counties has saturated
the ground. Rainfall has not been as significant further to the
west and northwest. That said, periods of showers and
thunderstorms are anticipated through this evening in association
with the remnants of Edouard. Embedded, training rain rates
between 2-4 inches per hour are possible in this deep tropical
airmass. Where this occurs, especially over the already hardest
hit areas, rainfall will rapidly runoff to produce flash
flooding. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop. Stay weather

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 3 at 3:42AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A strong front moved toward the Kuskokwim Delta coast overnight.
Southerly onshore winds gusting up to 40 mph coupled with a
lengthy fetch will promote elevated water levels 1 to 2 feet above
normal high tide through early this morning morning. Strongest
winds are expected to peak this morning, with up to 0.5 inches of
rainfall. Areas of the coastline that are perpendicular to the
southerly wind direction, such as Kwigillingok, have a higher
chance of seeing impacts with this front. Strong southerly winds
will continue through this afternoon and evening before slowly
diminishing through tonight.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to 108 expected.

* WHERE...The Rolling Plains and the far southeastern Texas
Panhandle.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 8 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: Crittenden; DeSoto; Shelby
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 3 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for today. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: GUSTY WINDS AND MODERATE TO HEAVY RAIN EXPECTED

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:13PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move into Western Alaska Wednesday evening into Thursday, with
widespread rain and gusty winds expected. Water levels late
Thursday through Saturday morning could rise 1 to 2 feet above
the normal high tide line along the Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...Late Thursday September 3 through Saturday September 5.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur. Heavy rain and
gusty winds could make travel difficult at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels are expected to peak late
Thursday into early Friday and again Saturday morning. Gusty
east/southeast winds Wednesday night will shift to the
south/southwest Thursday into Friday, leading to more onshore
flow and the potential for higher water levels. Strongest wind
gusts across the West Coast will peak on Thursday around 30 to
50 mph, with around 0.50 to 1.25 inches of rain expected through
Thursday night. Winds will be lighter Friday and Saturday, but
will remain onshore.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 2 at 3:26PM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for Thursday. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Beaverhead National Forest
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 1 at 10:22AM MDT until September 3 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON WEDNESDAY TO 8 PM MDT
THURSDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR EAST BEAVERHEAD...

.Strong southwest winds will develop Wednesday as a cold front tracks
eastward and stalls along the Continental Divide. Winds will peak
each afternoon and early evening. Winds will remain elevated
Wednesday night, especially across midslopes and ridgetops, with poor
humidity recoveries.

The National Weather Service in Missoula MT has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 111.

* TIMING...From noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 20 to 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

Make and maintain your go kit. Is it ready to go? Are there any
materials you need to refresh? Visit ready.gov/kit.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

NWSheadline: RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON WEDNESDAY TO 8 PM MDT THURSDAY
